title: The Koan Wall
intro: Thirty original lines, sorted into four families. Every line here is Wade's own writing, which makes this the only wing of the museum with a clean rights position on its own words.

families.name: Diagnostics
lines: Feeling isn't thinking. Memes aren't arguments.
A meme is not a method.
Don't confuse dopamine with discourse.
Don't mistake the feeling you get from a meme for thinking.
Memes: where emotion dresses up as insight.
Your fears become memes.
Your memes become manias.

families.name: Koans
families.voice: The ones that refuse the dopamine hit. The anti-memes proper.
lines: I always say what I meme. I never meme what I say.
There's no time like the internet.
It's emojis all the way down.
I know I said it, but I didn't meme it.
I know your avatar better than I know you.
In the land of the bling, the one memed man is king.
Please don't say anything that exceeds my capacity to represent it with emojis.
families.note: The last line is the strongest in the corpus: funny, a complete argument about emotional vocabulary, and it takes three seconds longer to land than a meme is supposed to take. That delay is the product.

families.name: Institutional voice
families.voice: Museum signage. Already partly live on the site.
lines: Outbreak level: high.
Proceed with critical thinking. Avoid sharing on an empty stomach.
All artifacts reserved.
Meme archaeologist.
I survived Rage Comics.
Eating brains since 2005.

families.name: Allusions
families.voice: Work by pointing at a known text. Titles aren't copyrightable, so the lines are usable, but each carries its source in the label — the attribution is not a legal hedge, it is the joke.
families.product_line: Prints, with attribution set as part of the design.

lines.text: The internet: because everyone wants to be alone together.

excluded.reason: This is Barbara Kruger's actual artwork, not a style reference. Cut entirely, including any meme-variant parenthetical. Her white-Futura-Bold-Oblique-on-red visual grammar is a style and available; her specific texts are not.

Register entry M14. KC Green sells merch from those exact panels. Printing the phrase competes directly with the author's own market. Discuss the meme in the museum by name — see content/specimens/m14-this-is-fine.json — never print the phrase.
